newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen tops Shanghai in listings so far in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen tops Shanghai in listings so far in 1997.

text.p: The Shenzhen Stock Exchange has listed more companies and registered larger turnover than rival Shanghai Stock Exchange so far in 1997, official statistics released on Monday showed.
Shenzhen received 42 new listings from the beginning of 1997 to April 18, while Shanghai only listed 16 companies, figures provided by the Shenzhen stock exchange indicated.
This boosted the number of Shenzhen-listed companies to 277, compared with 309 listed in Shanghai, the exchange said.
Shenzhen had 14.70 billion outstanding A shares while Shanghai had 15.32 billion as of April 18. For outstanding B shares, Shenzhen had 3.49 billion compared with Shanghai's 4.62 billion.
Share and fund turnover in Shenzhen was 586.13 billion yuan in the period, exceeding the 494.35 billion registered in Shanghai.
Figures also showed Shenzhen was closing the gap with Shanghai in terms of customer stock accounts.
The Shenzhen exchange gained 1.80 million new A share accounts from the start of the year to April 18, bringing the total to 12.79 million.
By March 31, Shanghai had 1.19 million new A share accounts for a total of 13.21 million, according to the statistics.
By April 18, Shenzhen had a total of 97,300 B share accounts with 3,700 added so far in 1997, the statistics showed. No figures were given for the Shanghai exchange.
